Note 6 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:

  - comment: Security DB record for Richard Davis (E011) shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training (never admin). Basic training means maximum is read. Requested write is above maximum, so recommend read.
reason: The Security agent looked up Richard Davis (E011) in its own database and reports employment type: contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training (never admin). Basic training means the maximum level is read. Note 6 from Security agent says: Security DB shows Richard Davis is a contractor with basic security training. Recommendation: read.

Hmm. The employer type conflict matters. Which to trust? Let me think about the policy.

The access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

If full-time Payroll Specialist: write is at/below max, grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max is read, so grant read.
